name: Juventus 2014–19
scopeNote: Focused run to check the Squad-axis (bas) anchor: only squad-building (and the manager's stated view, when found) was researched. Every other dimension is a gap, not evidence of absence. Partial dates: exact first and last match dates were not verified.
openQuestions: The anchor is the club's signing policy as much as Allegri's choices: is Juventus 2014–19 an Experience anchor for who gets minutes, or for who gets bought?

sources.title: Alteration in transfer policy heralds the start of a new era for Juventus (James Cormack)
sources.evidence: In Allegri's final season "they were beaten by a vibrant Ajax side boasting an average age of 21.5"; "The Juve squad, on average, was eight years older than Erik ten Hag's team."

sources.title: Same article, figure outside the period
sources.evidence: "In Serie A last season, Juve's squad boasted the highest average age (29.7)": 'last season' is 2019/20 (Sarri), not Allegri. Policy "based around buying the finished and perhaps peaking product" (no dates).

sources.title: Furious Allegri clashes with Italian media after Coppa Italia win (SI)
sources.evidence: Press framing: the 4-0 win "could represent the end of an era, given that several Juve players are now in their 30s."

sources.title: Search summary (newsghana, via Sportsmail)
sources.evidence: Summary only: lineup vs Monaco averaged 30 years 64 days. The summary named Pirlo and Evra, who left in 2015, so the season is doubtful.

statedView.quote: A team that wins seven titles in a row has no issues.

confidence.reason: Only squad-building researched; tier C sources, mostly press framing.
